chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Lester's tone and the band's hard reeds
summary: Smith says Lester kept an alto tone on tenor with a stiff reed, and the saxes used C-melody and baritone reeds to compete with the brass.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: One thing interesting about Lester is that he got that very sort of light sound on tenor, which was quite different from
Buster Smith - 43
Hawk.
Yes.
It was much more sort of floating over the changes rather than running straight through them, which is what Hawk would do.
Uh-huh.
Why was it, since he was so different...?
He's an old alto player, and he never did try to improve his tone...to get that tenor tone. He just stayed with that alto tone.
I love that tone.
Yeah. And he had a stiff reed, kept it on his tenor all the time.
I think it was Buddy Tate who said that one time he used to play with a plastic reed.
Yeah. I imagine he did.
Is that possible?
Oh yeah.
Because that's a real stiff reed, isn't it.
Yeah, a stiff reed. See, most of the time we didn't have but three saxes in the band. Lester Young, Theodore Ross and myself.
So two altos and a tenor.
Yes.
Did you have a trombone player at that time?
Buster Smith - 44
Yeah, yeah! We had two trombone players. We had two trombone players and three trumpets. And see, the saxophones tried to blow as loud as the trumpets played.
So they all had hard reeds.
Yeah. The alto player, we would get C-melody reeds and put them on an alto.
Did you have to cut them down to fit? Or did they fit the mouthpiece?
Yeah, they fit on it all right. Then Lester Young got to getting some baritone reeds and putting them on his tenor. So they'd blow as loud as the brass section would play.

It's very interesting, because when you listen to Lester's sound, and indeed to yours, it's got this lovely, light, floating quality, and I don't connect it with a hard reed at all. It doesn't sound as if it's a hard reed.
Yes.
You know, when you hear those guys booting away, like Hawk used to, you think, 'Now, that would be a hard reed.'
No. That's a soft reed.
Really.
Yeah. You can't get that big tone unless you got a soft reed. A #2. But a #3, #4 or #5, something like that, that's a hard reed. Yeah.
